rationale: Water damage to the policyholder's own home (basement flooring, drywall, contents) caused by failure of the policyholder's own plumbing system is a direct property damage claim.
claim_summary: Policyholder returned from work trip to find basement flooded with approximately two inches of water caused by a burst supply line under the upstairs bathroom sink that ran for roughly two days. Damage includes buckled hardwood flooring, soaked drywall up to one foot high, and ruined stored boxes throughout the basement. Estimated damage in the medium range ($2,000–$25,000).

case_facts.description: Two inches of water across entire basement, buckled hardwood floor, soaked drywall up to one foot, ruined stored boxes
case_facts.cause: burst supply line under upstairs bathroom sink, ran for approximately two days

rationale: Wind damage to the policyholder's own roof structure (shingles on back porch overhang) is straightforward property damage to the home.
claim_summary: Policyholder Jordan Lee (POL-1006) reported four shingles blown off the back porch overhang due to wind damage last weekend. Estimated repair cost is $400 with no water intrusion. Note: claim amount is below the $2,500 deductible, likely resulting in no coverage payout.

case_facts.damage_description: four shingles blown off, no water intrusion
